title: A small cross-hospital gain from an age–systolic-pressure interaction was not robust to source-sample uncertainty
abstract: In UCI historical coronary referral cohorts, a fixed age-by-resting-systolic-pressure product added to flexible additive standard measures reduced Hungarian target Brier loss from0.153235 to0.150576 after Cleveland training (303 source,294 target records). Source cross-validation worsened slightly. A2000-replicate joint source/target refit bootstrap gave a95% interval of-0.012882 to+0.014540 for target improvement. The modest observed transport gain therefore does not establish a stable predictor. Target data were independently sampled by hospital but historically reused, not lifetime untouched. Author self-checks and isolated reruns were performed; no independent peer review or clinical validation is claimed.
